body:
As far as my `bisect` goes, this was introduced [here](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/commit/f50135a32e11c535e1dc3a8e9460c5b4e640ee86), and the issue comes with how `fugitive` uses `tempname()` to create a `.sh` file (see [here](https://github.com/tpope/vim-fugitive/blob/f809dde0e719f89a6fb5cb80f3be65f5cbc1d1fe/autoload/fugitive.vim#L260)) that is then passed to `git` via the environment as the `GIT_EDITOR` (see [here](https://github.com/tpope/vim-fugitive/blob/f809dde0e719f89a6fb5cb80f3be65f5cbc1d1fe/autoload/fugitive.vim#L3828)).

Somewhere along the lines things are getting messed up - **and I understand that there are a whole slew of things going on here that make it almost impossible to handle edge-case wise**.

---

Raising as issue more-so for **feedback on how to circumvent this in my own config**, as from what I can see the addition of the `$USER` to the return of `tempname()` is not something that can be overridden. I cannot edit the username on the system where I am running into issues.

> As far as my `bisect` goes, this was introduced [here](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/commit/f50135a32e11c535e1dc3a8e9460c5b4e640ee86),

Yes. Thanks for debugging and reporting this!

One way to fix this is for `vim_mktempdir()` to replace special chars in the username part of the tempname path. https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/c84ae5706fb0c31c415fedbc15021e9b2ef46065/src/nvim/fileio.c#L5313

Would ~the change mentioned above and~ tests in `fileio_spec.lua` be enough for a PR @justinmk? I'm happy to take a stab at it ~if this is truly that simple~.

---

Edit: I think I misread your comment above - you were just referencing the line where things need to change.

Are there already functions to escape strings that could be used to pre-process `user` here? I'm aware of `fnameescape` from the VimL side, which I imagine has some backing function in the C code?
btw does the result of `:lua =vim.loop.os_homedir()` match your username or what form does it take? Wondering if `vim_mktempdir` should use `os_homedir` instead of `os_get_username`.

>Can you try this patch

Will do ASAP and report back here.

---

>btw does the result of :lua =vim.loop.os_homedir() match your username or what form does it take? Wondering if vim_mktempdir should use os_homedir instead of os_get_username

In the example given above with a user `foo\\bar` (normally printed as `foo\bar`), the output of `:lua print(vim.loop.os_homedir())` is just `bar`, which matches `$HOME` (without `/home/`). The `foo` in this example is a "namespace", so using whatever is after the `\` seems like a good solution. Not sure about edge cases, but it seems like that would at least always be a valid path.

@justinmk the above patch does not work, but sanity check what I'm doing here:

```
git clone git@github.com:neovim/neovim.git
cd neovim
git apply jmk.patch
```

at this point `git status` shows:

```

```

continuing then:

```

sudo make install
```

after which, `:version` from `/usr/local/bin/nvim` yields:

```

and then:

```
sudo su - foo\\bar
cd tmp-project
rm -rf /tmp/neovim; ~/nvim --noplugin -u /tmp/init.lua
```

then `:G`, and an `cc` yields:

```
sh: /tmp/nvim.foobar/RfYHrd/1.sh: No such file or directory                                                                                                                                                                         
error: There was a problem with the editor 'sh /tmp/nvim.foo\bar/RfYHrd/1.sh'.
Please supply the message using either -m or -F option.
Press ENTER or type command to continue```

>you can skip make install and just use ./build/bin/nvim after make.

It's a bit weird because I have to switch users. I believe my runtime files were super out of date as well (I usually use the `appimage`) as I was getting issues with `vim.lsp` not existing. Now that the runtime stuff is updated via one `make install` though, I imagine newer builds will work? We will see though. Thanks for the advice either way.

---

In the previous set of steps, I was running `nvim` via:

```
rm -rf /tmp/neovim; ~/nvim --noplugin -u /tmp/init.lua
```

noting the use of `~/nvim`, which is just the `appimage` from a few days ago. This should be `/usr/local/bin/nvim` which is the version built locally.

With that in mind (and corrected) @justinmk:

* The first provided patch continues to not solve the problem
* The second provided patch _does_ solve the issue
You think the second patch is a viable solution @justinmk? If so, I'm happy to throw that in a PR with some tests and submit it.
